enriched_description: Single-wheeled vehicle with pedals directly attached to the wheel hub. Wheel diameter ranges from 12 inches (children's) to 36 inches (performance). Frame consists of a seat post rising from the wheel fork, terminating in a saddle seat. Crank arms extend from the hub with flat pedals. No handlebars or steering mechanism - balance is controlled by body position. Frame is steel or aluminum in various colors. Tire is narrow with a smooth or lightly treaded surface. Overall height 60-120 cm depending on wheel size.

Vertical piano with a tall rectangular cabinet approximately 110-140 cm high, 140-150 cm wide, 55-65 cm deep. Front panel opens to reveal 88 keys (52 white, 36 black) arranged in the standard chromatic pattern. Music stand extends from the top front. Three pedals (soft, sostenuto, sustain) protrude from the base. Cabinet is finished in polished ebony, mahogany, or walnut. Interior strings run vertically behind the keys. Soundboard is visible through the open front. Legs are short and blocky. Overall silhouette is tall and narrow compared to grand pianos.

Electric cleaning appliance with a body housing a motor and dust collection system. Upright models have a tall handle extending from a rectangular cleaning head with a rotating brush roll. Canister models have a compact body on wheels with a flexible hose and wand attachment. Color is typically white, gray, red, or blue. Dust bag or bagless cyclone container is visible. Power cord extends from the rear (6-10 meters). Cleaning head has bristles and a suction opening. Controls on the handle include power switch and brush roll on/off. Weight 3-8 kg.

Open decorative container with a narrow neck and wider body, designed to hold cut flowers. Height ranges from 15-50 cm. Shape varies: cylindrical, bulbous, tapered, or fluted. Material is glass (transparent, frosted, or colored), ceramic (glazed or unglazed), porcelain, or metal. Surface may feature painted patterns, etched designs, or a smooth monochrome finish. Opening at the top is circular or oval, 3-10 cm in diameter. Base is flat and stable. Glass vases show water level when filled. Ceramic vases have an unglazed foot ring on the bottom.

Arched architectural ceiling or roof constructed from brick, stone, or concrete blocks. Arch forms a continuous curved surface spanning between walls or piers. Types include barrel vault (single continuous arch), groin vault (intersecting barrel vaults), and ribbed vault (arches supported by stone ribs). Surface shows individual masonry units with mortar joints. Color reflects the material: warm terracotta for brick, gray for stone, white for plaster-finished. The arch creates a sense of height and grandeur. Interior surface may be decorated with frescoes or coffered patterns.

Luxurious fabric with a dense pile of evenly cut short fibers creating a smooth soft surface. Pile height is 1-3 mm, giving a plush tactile quality. Surface has a characteristic sheen that changes appearance depending on the viewing angle (light reflects differently from the nap direction). Color is rich and saturated: deep red, royal blue, emerald green, black, or gold. Back side is a plain weave without pile. Fabric drapes heavily and folds in soft rounded creases. Crushed velvet shows an irregular pattern where the pile has been pressed in different directions.

Tall rectangular dispensing machine with a glass front displaying rows of products (snacks, beverages, or other goods). Body is metal (steel) painted in brand colors. Glass panel reveals product coils or shelves behind it. Payment interface includes a bill acceptor, coin slot, and/or card reader on the front panel. Product selection keypad has numbered buttons. Dispensing tray is at the bottom front. Overall dimensions approximately 180 cm tall, 90 cm wide, 80 cm deep. Interior lighting illuminates the products. LED display shows price and selection information.

Ceremonial religious garment worn by clergy during worship services. Typically a long flowing robe or chasuble made from rich fabric (silk, brocade, damask) in liturgical colors (white, red, green, purple, gold). Surface features embroidered crosses, symbols, or decorative borders. Shape is wide and open, draping over the shoulders and extending to the ankles. Some versions have an orphrey (decorative band) running down the front and back. Fabric has a lustrous sheen. Worn over an alb (white undergarment). Stole may be draped around the neck.

Long bridge-like structure consisting of a series of arches or spans supported by tall piers or columns. Extends across a valley, road, or railway. Individual arches are semicircular or segmental, constructed from stone, brick, or concrete. Piers are massive rectangular or cylindrical columns spaced at regular intervals (10-30 meters apart). Deck runs continuously across the top of the arches. Overall length can exceed 500 meters. Height varies with the terrain being crossed. Color reflects construction material: gray concrete, red brick, or natural stone.

Bowed stringed instrument with a curved wooden body approximately 35 cm long. Body has an hourglass shape with C-bouts (inward curves) on each side. Top plate (soundboard) is spruce with two f-shaped sound holes. Back plate is maple with a distinctive flame pattern. Four strings (G, D, A, E) run from a tailpiece at the base over a bridge to tuning pegs in the scroll. Neck extends from the body to a carved scroll at the top. Fingerboard is ebony (black). Varnish finish is amber, reddish-brown, or golden. Chin rest is attached at the lower left. Bow is a wooden stick with horsehair.
